title: Edge Case
definition: An edge case is a valid or invalid scenario near a behavioral boundary where ordinary assumptions are most likely to fail.
purpose: Teach systematic boundary discovery without treating every unusual input as the same class.
history: Boundary analysis and testing practices emphasize values and conditions where behavior changes or assumptions break.
mental_model: An edge case stands near a seam in the problem contract where two rules, limits, or assumptions meet.
analogy: Testing a door at the exact closing point reveals boundary behavior, but software boundaries may involve time, permissions, concurrency, and data rather than a physical edge.
common_mistakes: Calling every invalid value an edge case
industry_notes: Boundary-focused review finds failures hidden by happy-path examples.
ai_notes: AI-generated test lists must be checked against the actual valid domain and authoritative constraints.
interview_notes: Ask the candidate to distinguish normal, boundary, edge, and invalid scenarios.
exercise_candidates: Classify scenarios by validity and boundary relation
lab_candidates: Build a scenario matrix for ticket pricing
project_candidates: Define project edge cases before implementation
